[PEDIGREE & GENETIC ANALYSIS] In a family pedigree tracing hair patterns, two parents with curly hair have an offspring with straight hair. 1) Deduce which allele is dominant and explain your reasoning. 2) If these curly-haired parents have another child, calculate the theoretical probability that the child will have straight hair.
rubric: To score full points, the response must demonstrate structural mastery: 1) The allele for curly hair is dominant. Because both parents exhibit curly hair but produce a straight-haired child, the parents must be heterozygous. Under heterozygous conditions, only the dominant allele expresses itself physically, while the recessive allele is masked. 2) The theoretical probability of having a straight-haired child (homozygous recessive) from a standard heterozygous monohybrid cross (Aa x Aa) is 1/4 or 25%.
